title: Lamb Biryani
subtitle: Slow-cooked spiced lamb layered with fragrant rice
excerpt: Biryani is one of the great celebratory dishes of the Indian subcontinent. This version layers part-cooked basmati rice over a spiced lamb base, then seals the pot and lets everything steam together so the rice absorbs the meat juices. It takes time, but the result is impressive.
sourceNotes: Biryani arrived in the Indian subcontinent with the Mughals and the Persian-influenced courts of the Deccan. The dum technique -- sealing the pot and cooking over low heat -- is central to every regional style, from Hyderabadi to Lucknowi to Sindhi.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the lamb overnight for deeper flavour. The fried onions can be made 1 day ahead.

content.text: The most important step is par-cooking the rice to exactly 70 percent done before layering. Overcooked rice will turn mushy during the dum. Taste a grain -- it should have a firm, chalky centre. The saffron milk gives the finished dish its golden streaks.

items.prepNote: made into a paste with the ginger
made into a paste with the garlic
use 4 green cardamom pods, lightly crushed
steeped in 4 tbsp warm milk for 15 minutes

content.text: Mix the lamb with the yoghurt, garlic-ginger paste, garam masala, cinnamon, cardamom, and salt. Marinate for at least 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge.
Fry the sliced onions in the oil over medium-high heat for 20 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper. Set aside.
Cook the marinated lamb in the same oil over high heat for 5 minutes. Reduce to medium, add 200ml of water, cover, and braise for 40 minutes until the lamb is just tender and the sauce is thick.
Cook the drained rice in a large pot of heavily salted boiling water for 5 minutes until 70 percent cooked. Drain well.

Layer in a large heavy pot: spread the lamb base first, then half the rice, then half the fried onions. Drizzle over half the saffron milk. Add the remaining rice, the rest of the onions, and the remaining saffron milk. Dot the butter over the top.
Seal the pot tightly with foil, then place the lid on top. Cook in the oven at 150 degrees for 30 minutes, or on the lowest hob heat for 30 minutes using a heat diffuser.
Rest for 15 minutes without opening. Serve by scooping through the layers so each portion has both rice and lamb.

items.cause: Par-cooked for too long before layering
items.fix: Rice should have a firm chalky centre at the boiling stage -- aim for 5 minutes maximum

items.cause: Heat too high during the dum stage
items.fix: Use the lowest possible heat and a heavy-bottomed pot; a heat diffuser is a big help
Add 100ml of water and braise for another 20 minutes before layering

content.text: Biryani is food for festivals, weddings, and celebrations across Pakistan, India, and Bangladesh. Every major city and region has its own version. Hyderabad, Lucknow, Kolkata, Sindh, and Karachi all claim a definitive style. What they share is the dum technique and the use of fragrant basmati rice.
